main_body: Roofed stone well with a snow-covered roof, wooden posts, a dark water opening with a bucket, and a stone base
top_band: Snow roof: white and pale blue, rows 1-8 (about 7 rows), with a lighter front edge at row 8 and icicles below. The well rim is mid-grey stone at rows 14-16 around the dark opening.
evidence: Down the middle column: the snow roof reads as a lighter surface (rows 1-8) that ends in a front edge and icicles. Below it the stone rim surrounds a dark elliptical opening (rows 16-22) with a bucket inside, so the opening is visible from above. The banded stone front face continues below (rows 24-30). The opening is inset, with a stone lip around it. The roof and opening are both horizontal surfaces seen from above, so the piece follows the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The snow has about 4-5 steps (white, pale blue, blue-grey, shadow blue). The wood posts have 3-4 brown steps. The stone has dithered grey speckle and dark banding, so no large flat areas. Outlines are dark brown or dark blue-grey and lean toward the neighbouring material, not black. It is comparable to the roofed-well reference, though the lower stone is a little more repetitive and slightly less rich per tile.
